summary: Specifies the wais URI scheme, originally defined in RFC 1738. It was written so RFC 1738 could be made obsolete while keeping information about the scheme on record. This document is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4156 records how a wais URI identifies a WAIS database, a search, or a document in a database. The RFC is Historic and notes that WAIS was not widely implemented and almost no WAIS servers were in use at the time.

subtitle: The URI forms used to identify WAIS databases, searches, and documents.

tldr.problem: The definition of the wais URI scheme was in RFC 1738, which was being made obsolete while information about the scheme needed to be retained.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC records three wais URL forms for databases, searches, and documents, including the default port when it is omitted.
tldr.outcome: The document preserves the scheme definition and notes that WAIS was not widely implemented and almost no servers were in use at publication; the unit marks it Historic.

today: The unit metadata marks RFC 4156 as Historic. The RFC notes that almost no WAIS servers were in use at the time it was written.

sections.title: Why the Scheme Was Recorded Again
sections.content:
Many URI schemes were first defined in RFC 1738. Because that document had become obsolete, RFC 4156 copies the wais scheme definition so information about it remains available.

The RFC describes the scheme as identifying WAIS databases, searches, and individual documents in a WAIS database. It says the scheme is not intended for arbitrary Z39.50 services.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC preserves the wais address format after its earlier source document became obsolete. The format identifies resources offered through WAIS.

sections.title: Three Forms of a WAIS URI
sections.content:
A wais URI can name a database, a specific search in that database, or a particular document. The document form includes the WAIS object type and an opaque document identifier that only the server that issued it can interpret.

If the port is omitted, the default is 210. The type in a document URI gives the client information that some WAIS implementations require to retrieve the object.
sections.plainLanguage: The address can point to a database, a search, or one document. The document identifier is for the WAIS server to interpret, not for clients to take apart.

sections.title: Security and Historical Context
sections.content:
The RFC says the WAIS protocol specifies neither privacy nor authentication. It also notes that the protocol was not widely implemented and that almost no WAIS servers were in use at the time of writing.

The unit metadata marks this document Historic. RFC 4156 records the URI syntax rather than defining a new WAIS protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The URI scheme does not add privacy or authentication to WAIS. The RFC records a historical format for a protocol that had little deployment at the time.
